blocks.heading: Product life cycle
blocks.text: A product life cycle describes the stages a product passes through from introduction, through growth and maturity, and finally decline. It is a model of sales through time, not a promise of identical timing for every product. Introduction commonly involves low initial sales and awareness-building; growth brings rising sales; maturity involves slower growth or a plateau; decline involves falling sales. Development can precede introduction, but sales have not yet begun. Managers can use evidence to consider changes, while recognising a temporary fall does not prove permanent decline.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Tula Bottles observes an established range’s sales flattening after earlier growth. The pattern could suggest maturity, but management should examine competition, availability and actual data before choosing a response.
